newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. spot resids hold, buoyed by firm gas.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. spot resids hold, buoyed by firm gas.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly were little changed again Monday in quiet trade, with firm East Coast city gate gas quotes still supporting the complex despite the lack of weather-related demand.

"Gas has been strong and there's still some oil going to Mexico. I just don't see resid falling much right now," said one cash trader, noting there were not a lot of surplus barrels around, particularly high sulphur material, despite the mild weather that had slowed utility burns.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent held steady at $16.50-75 a barrel, with September one percent paper talked 20 cents lower at $16.20-40 with softer crude.
NYH prompt 0.3 percent high pour was down slightly to the $18.25-50 area, pressured by a lack of utility demand.
High sulphurs in New York were steady to up slightly, with 2.2 percent now quoted in the low-$16s, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable to firmer, with one percent still at $16.50 and three percent flat to up slightly in the low-$16s.
Traders said they expected a major to sell another 45-50,000 barrels of prompt USG 2.8 percent in the $16.40 area, up from $16 reported for a piece Friday.

New York city gate swing prices gained a couple of cents Monday to the mid-$2.70s/mmBtu, or $17.39 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed three cents to the mid-$2.50s/mmBtu, or about $16.07 a barrel.
